You are a fix worker on the OBE podcast repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast - edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, branch, or push; leave changes uncommitted. No skills/MCP/network. Use PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 for all python.

WHY (deny-by-default safety hole, confirmed by a read-only diagnosis): server/pipeline/content_edit.py find_content_cuts() is the MANDATORY content-safety gate for publishing. Today it fails OPEN on malformed model output. json.loads accepts any JSON type (content_edit.py ~208-210); parse_cut_list() turns a non-list OR malformed rows into [] (content_edit.py ~76-96); then find_content_cuts stamps that empty result {cuts:[], max_severity:0, hold:False, ok:True} (content_edit.py ~262-269). So a safety-model response of the WRONG SHAPE - e.g. the object {"ok": false}, a bare string/number/bool, JSON null already handled elsewhere, or an array whose rows are all malformed/dropped - is silently reported as VERIFIED CLEAN, NO CUTS. That is a fail-open in the gate that decides whether an episode can publish. It must fail CLOSED instead.

HARD INVARIANT (never violate): an unverifiable, malformed, wrong-schema, empty-after-drop, or model-unavailable safety result must NEVER become ok:true with cuts:[]. It must become ok:false, hold:true (route to human review) OR raise. A genuine, well-formed safety result with severity below threshold legitimately returns ok:true, hold:false, cuts:[] - that path must still work. Do not weaken the gate; only stop malformed output from masquerading as clean.

OWNERSHIP - you own ONLY these three files, never touch anything else (especially NOT server/pipeline/editorial_plan.py source):
- server/pipeline/content_edit.py
- tests/test_content_edit.py
- tests/test_editorial_plan.py

BUILD:
1. Add a small dedicated validator beside parse_cut_list, e.g. `def _validate_content_cut_payload(data) -> bool`: returns True only when `data` is a list AND every element is a dict carrying the safety-cut required fields (at minimum coercible start_s and end_s; also require a severity that coerces to a number and a non-empty reason/category IF the existing well-formed safety rows in this codebase carry them - inspect parse_cut_list and the existing tests to match the real schema, do not invent fields). An empty list is VALID (it means the model genuinely returned no cuts) - return True for []. Any non-list, or any list containing a non-dict row or a row missing required coercible fields, returns False.
2. In find_content_cuts, immediately after the raw model result is obtained from the shared runner (the `raw = _run_editor_llm(...)` result, around content_edit.py ~256, BEFORE calling parse_cut_list to build the returned cuts), branch: if raw is None keep the existing fail-closed {..., hold:True, ok:False} behavior (unchanged); else if `_validate_content_cut_payload(raw)` is False, return a fail-closed dict {"cuts": [], "max_severity": 0, "hold": True, "ok": False, "reason": "content-safety response failed schema validation"} (mirror the exact key set of the existing hold:true/ok:false return so callers are unaffected). Only when the payload validates do you proceed to parse_cut_list + severity/hold computation and the existing ok:True return.
3. Keep parse_cut_list(data) unchanged as a pure lenient normalizer - other callers (the POLISH pass find_editorial_cuts) rely on its leniency and polish is allowed to soft-skip. Do NOT make parse_cut_list itself strict; do the strict validation only in the SAFETY entry point find_content_cuts.
4. Do NOT touch server/pipeline/editorial_plan.py at all. Its lines 290-291 (raise EditorialPlanBlocked on ok:false/non-dict) and 292-293 (raise on ok:true+hold:true) are correct and must stay. Your change only affects what find_content_cuts RETURNS.
5. Do NOT rely on PLACEHOLDER_MODE for any assertion of production safety; tests must run with PLACEHOLDER_MODE unset.

TESTS - add to the two owned test files (mock the model; NO real Claude/orchestrator/network/media). Use these EXACT test function names so the check can find them:
- in tests/test_content_edit.py: `def test_find_content_cuts_schema_mismatch_fails_closed`: monkeypatch the editor call so the safety model returns valid JSON of the WRONG shape (cover at least the object {"ok": false} and an all-malformed-rows array); assert find_content_cuts returns ok is False, hold is True, and cuts == [] (NOT ok:true). Also assert that a genuine well-formed EMPTY cut array still returns ok:true, hold:false, cuts:[] (the legitimate no-cuts path is preserved).
- in tests/test_editorial_plan.py: `def test_build_episode_edit_plan_blocks_incomplete_content_safety`: override the autouse safety stub with {"cuts": [], "max_severity": 0, "hold": True, "ok": False}; assert pytest.raises(EditorialPlanBlocked, match="content-safety analysis did not complete"); and assert the downstream angle_render.build_edit_plan was NOT called (spy/monkeypatch) - i.e. no plan is produced from an incomplete safety result.
- keep/add a distinct test that a well-formed ok:true + hold:true safety result raises the SEPARATE "content-safety gate requires human review" message, so the substantive-hold path stays distinct from the incomplete path.
- ALL existing tests in both files must stay green; if any existing test asserted the OLD fail-open behavior (e.g. a non-list coerced to ok:true clean), update it to the fail-closed contract and list which in your summary.

HOW TO RUN (this is exactly what the grader runs):
env -u PLACEHOLDER_MODE PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_content_edit.py tests/test_editorial_plan.py

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave changes uncommitted; write ./fix-summary.md with headings '# Fix Summary','## Summary','## Files Changed','## Verification','## Assumptions' (<600 words). In Verification, paste the pytest summary line and name every existing test you modified and why.
